question.problem:
Find the equation of the **normal** line to the polar curve $r=1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ at $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ given that

$$
{y}^{′}(\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14225095/assets/fc3ec38b91c71be3e9638dfa0127f1baab5d11d30e6156d863b36758f6751e7d.png)

Find the equation of the **normal** line to the polar curve $r = 1 - 2\cos\theta$ at $\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{2},$ given that

$$
y'(\theta)  = \cos\theta-2\cos(2\theta) , \qquad
x'(\theta) = 2\sin(2\theta) - \sin\theta.
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the normal line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}.$

In this case, we're given that

$$
y'(\theta)  = \cos\theta-2\cos(2\theta) , \qquad
x'(\theta) = 2\sin(2\theta) - \sin\theta.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P.$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =3\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}))}{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\pi ))}{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))} \\  & =\frac{0-2(-1)}{0-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{0+2}{0+1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P.$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & =(1-2\cdot 0)\cdot 0 \\  & =0 \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & =(1-2\cdot 0)\cdot (-1) \\  & =1\cdot (-1) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $\left( 0, -1 \right).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the normal.

We find the equation of the normal as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{m}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-1) & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (x-0) \\ y+1 & =-\frac{1}{2}x \\ y & =-\frac{1}{2}x-1\end{aligned}
$$
